card: Bitcoin Core checks whether existing block data is obfuscated before creating a null XOR key when blocks/xor.dat is missing, failing startup if obfuscated files are found without a key. Currently, a missing key file causes the node to silently write an all-zero key, falsely report database corruption, and silently discard the chain down to height 0 if restarted with -reindex. The author demonstrates reproducible chain loss and silent reset under -reindex on master. The change preserves intact block storage so users can restore their key without data loss. There are no dependencies.
evidence: PR description provides a reproduction showing that after removing `xor.dat`, master reports "Corrupted block database detected", while `-reindex` completes with no error but leaves the node at height 0 with data discarded; restoring the key recovers height 20 cleanly if no reindex was run.
problem: When `blocks/xor.dat` is lost on a node with obfuscated block storage, the node silently writes an all-zero key and fails reads with a "Corrupted block database detected" error. Following the prompt to run `-reindex` silently discards the chain, resets the node to height 0 with no error, and overwrites the initial block file, making recovery difficult even if the original key is found.
summary: Prevents writing a null XOR key when `blocks/xor.dat` is missing if existing block files are already obfuscated. Node initialization inspects block file headers for network magic and aborts with an actionable error instead of silently defaulting to an all-zero key. This leaves block data intact so users can restore a lost key file rather than overwriting block files during a subsequent reindex.
